question: How do I create a kMeet meeting?
ground_truth: To create a kMeet meeting: 1) Start kMeet via kmeet.infomaniak.com or from the desktop/mobile app. 2) Start a new meeting. 3) Enter a name for your meeting room. 4) Allow access to webcam and microphone. 5) Enter your name or pseudonym. 6) Optionally enable participant control, password, or encryption. 7) Click 'Join the meeting'. 8) Share the room link to invite participants.
actual_response:
To create a kMeet meeting, follow these steps:

1. **Start kMeet**:
   - Go to [kmeet.infomaniak.com](https://kmeet.infomaniak.com) or use the kMeet application on your computer or mobile device.

2. **Create a new meeting**:
   - Click on the option to start a new meeting.

3. **Configure the meeting**:
   - Enter a **name** for your meeting room.
   - Allow access to your webcam and microphone.
   - Enter your **pseudonym** or **first and last name**.

4. **Set security options (optional)**:
   - Enable participant control, a password, or a custom encryption key if needed.

5. **Join the meeting**:
   - Click on **Join the meeting**.

6. **Invite participants**:
   - Share the meeting link with participants to invite them to join.

For more details, refer to the [official guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2475/create-a-kmeet-meeting).

question: How can I share my screen during a kMeet call?
ground_truth: To share your screen in kMeet: 1) Have the desktop app (macOS/Windows) or mobile app (Android) - screen sharing is not yet available on iOS. 2) Create or join a meeting. 3) Click on the screen icon with an arrow to 'Share your screen'. 4) Validate authorization to access screen content. 5) Choose to share the entire screen or a specific window. 6) Click button to start sharing. 7) To stop, click the toolbar icon again. Note: Permissions may require a restart on first use.
key_points: choose entire screen or specific window
actual_response:
To share your screen during a kMeet call, follow these steps:

1. Start kMeet via [kmeet.infomaniak.com](https://kmeet.infomaniak.com) or from one of the applications for computers or mobile devices.
2. Create or join a meeting room.
3. Click on the screen icon with an arrow to **Share your screen**.
4. Read the warning that may be displayed by your device and validate the authorization to access the screen content.
5. Choose whether to share your entire screen or a specific window.
6. Click the button to start the sharing.
7. To stop the broadcast, click again on the toolbar icon.

For more details, you can refer to the [official guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2477/share-your-screen-on-kmeet).

question: What should I do if my audio is not working in kMeet?
ground_truth: To fix audio issues in kMeet: 1) Go to kMeet Settings and reauthorize microphone access. 2) Check browser lock icon isn't blocking multimedia. 3) On mobile, check Settings > Privacy > Microphone permissions for kMeet. 4) On Windows, use Privacy settings and Audio Troubleshooter. 5) Try joining from a different device (mobile instead of computer or vice versa). 6) As last resort on Firefox, disable WebRTC in about:config by setting media.peerconnection.enabled to false.
actual_response:
If your audio is not working in kMeet, follow these steps to troubleshoot the issue:

### General Tips
1. **Reauthorize Multimedia Access**:
   - Go to **Settings** in kMeet (click the gear icon at the top right).
   - Ensure access to the microphone is enabled and select the correct device.
   - Check for a lock icon in your browser's address bar that might be blocking access and click it to adjust permissions.
   - Source: [Fix an audio issue on kMeet](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2441/fix-an-audio-issue-on-kmeet)

2. **Check Browser Settings**:
   - Ensure your browser allows access to the microphone.
   - If using Firefox, disable WebRTC as a last resort:
     - Open Firefox and type `about:config` in the address bar.
     - Find `media.peerconnection.enabled` and set it to `false`.
     - Source: [Fix an audio issue on kMeet](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2441/fix-an-audio-issue-on-kmeet)

3. **Join from a Different Device**:
   - If the issue persists, try joining the meeting from another device (e.g., switch from computer to mobile).
   - Source: [Fix an audio issue on kMeet](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2441/fix-an-audio-issue-on-kmeet)

### For Windows Users
1. **Check Privacy Settings**:
   - Go to **Windows Settings > Privacy**.
   - Ensure "Allow apps to access the camera" and "Allow apps to access the microphone" are enabled.
   - Enable permissions for "Windows Search," "Camera," and "App Connector."

2. **Run the Audio Troubleshooter**:
   - Search for "Audio Troubleshooter" in the taskbar.
   - Select "Find and fix problems playing sound" and follow the prompts.
   - Source: [Fix an audio issue on kMeet](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2441/fix-an-audio-issue-on-kmeet)

### For Mobile Users
1. **Check Permissions on iOS**:
   - Go to **Settings > Privacy & Security**.
   - Ensure kMeet has access to the microphone and camera.
   - Check for any restrictions in "Security Control."

2. **Check Permissions on Android**:
   - Go to **Settings > Apps > kMeet > Permissions**.
   - Ensure all necessary permissions (microphone, camera) are allowed.
   - Source: [Fix an audio issue on kMeet](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2441/fix-an-audio-issue-on-kmeet)

### Firewall Settings
- If you still can't hear others, check your firewall settings:
  - Allow UDP Protocol `443` and TCP port `443`.
  - Allow the following IP addresses:
    - `185.125.24.0/24` (TCP)
    - `185.125.24.0/24` (UDP)
  - Source: [Solving a problem on kMeet](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/289/solving-a-problem-on-kmeet)

If the issue persists, consider contacting Infomaniak support for further assistance.

question: How do I create side rooms (breakout rooms) in kMeet?
ground_truth: To create side rooms in kMeet: 1) You must be a moderator. 2) Start kMeet via kmeet.infomaniak.com or app. 3) Once participants are in the meeting, click on the multi-user icon in the toolbar. 4) Click the button to add a side room. 5) Participants can then join or leave the room. 6) The moderator can force participants to join a specific side room via the action menu. Side rooms allow dividing a main meeting into several simultaneous discussions in distinct virtual spaces.
key_points: moderator can force participants to join
actual_response:
To create side rooms (breakout rooms) in kMeet, follow these steps:

1. **Start kMeet as a moderator**: Open kMeet via [kmeet.infomaniak.com](https://kmeet.infomaniak.com) or use the kMeet application on your computer or mobile device.
2. **Join the meeting**: Ensure all participants are in the meeting.
3. **Access the side rooms feature**: Click on the multi-user icon in the kMeet toolbar.
4. **Create a side room**: Click the button to add a side room.
5. **Manage participants**: Participants can join the created room or leave it. The moderator can also force participants to join a side room by clicking on the action menu next to their name in the participant list.

For more details, refer to the [official guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2397/create-a-kmeet-meeting-side-room).

question: How can I record a kMeet meeting?
ground_truth: To record a kMeet meeting: Prerequisites: Have a kDrive, be the moderator, and don't use encrypted meeting with custom key. Steps: 1) Start kMeet. 2) Once in the meeting, click on the action menu (three dots). 3) Click 'Start recording'. 4) Log in to Infomaniak if needed and select a kDrive for storage. 5) To stop, click the toolbar again and choose 'Stop recording'. 6) The recording is saved to the kDrive root in .mp4 format when all participants leave. Maximum duration is 3 hours.
actual_response:
To record a kMeet meeting, follow these steps:

1. Start **kMeet** via [kmeet.infomaniak.com](https://kmeet.infomaniak.com) or from one of the apps for computers and mobile devices.
2. Once in the meeting, click on the action menu **○○○** in the kMeet toolbar.
3. Click on the icon ◉ **Start recording**.
4. Confirm the operation and, if necessary, log in to your Infomaniak account. Then, select a kDrive to record the video conference on and click the button to start.
5. To stop recording, click on the toolbar again, then choose **Stop recording**.
6. Confirm, then choose whether you want to go to the recording location on kDrive.
7. The recording will be available at the root of the chosen kDrive as soon as the virtual room in which the meeting was held is closed (i.e., as soon as all participants have left the video conference).

For more details, refer to the [official guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2472/save-a-kmeet-meeting-on-kdrive).

question: How do I set a password for my kMeet meeting?
ground_truth: To protect a kMeet meeting with a password: 1) Start kMeet via kmeet.infomaniak.com or app. 2) Start a new meeting. 3) Enter the meeting room name. 4) Click on 'security options'. 5) Enable the toggle switch to 'Protect access'. 6) Create the password. 7) Click Continue to start. 8) Share both the meeting link/code AND the password with participants. You can also enable end-to-end encryption from security options (works only with Chromium-based browsers).
actual_response:
To set a password for your kMeet meeting, follow these steps:

1. Start kMeet via [kmeet.infomaniak.com](https://kmeet.infomaniak.com) or from one of the applications for computers or mobile devices.
2. Start a new meeting.
3. Enter a **name** for your meeting room.
4. Click on the **security options**.
5. Enable the toggle switch to **Protect access**.
6. Create the password.
7. **Continue** to **start** the meeting.
8. Specify the name you want to use as a participant in the meeting.
9. Share the **meeting link or code** and the **password** with your participants.

You can review the password if necessary by inviting participants via the dedicated button.

For more details, refer to the [Infomaniak documentation](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2464/secure-a-kmeet-meeting-with-a-password-and-encryption-key).

question: How can I livestream a kMeet meeting?
ground_truth: To livestream a kMeet meeting: Prerequisites: Must be a moderator (no Video Streaming offer required). Steps: 1) Start kMeet via ksuite.infomaniak.com/kmeet or app. 2) Once in the meeting, click the action menu (three dots). 3) Choose 'Start live broadcast'. 4) Click 'Start' button. 5) Wait for Video Streaming to be created. 6) Copy the stream URL and share it with viewers. 7) A symbol and audio alert indicate the broadcast start. The stream is continuous for max 24 hours and stops when the kMeet meeting ends.
actual_response:
To livestream a kMeet meeting, follow these steps:

1. **Start the kMeet Meeting**:
   - Open kMeet via [ksuite.infomaniak.com/kmeet](https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/kmeet) or use the kMeet app on your computer or mobile device.

2. **Initiate the Live Broadcast**:
   - Once in the meeting, click on the action menu (**○○○**) in the kMeet toolbar.
   - Select **Start live broadcast**.

3. **Start the Stream**:
   - Click the **Start** button to begin the live broadcast.

4. **Share the Stream Link**:
   - Wait for the Video Streaming link to be generated.
   - Copy the URL provided and share it with participants or anyone who needs to attend the live broadcast.

5. **Monitor the Broadcast**:
   - A symbol and an audible alert will indicate that the broadcast is live.

The stream will continue for a maximum of 24 hours and will stop as soon as the kMeet meeting ends.

For more details, refer to the [official guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1355/broadcast-a-kmeet-meeting-via-live-streaming-mode).

question: How do I install kDrive on Linux?
ground_truth: To install kDrive on Linux: Prerequisites: Download the kDrive .AppImage file, install libfuse2 (required for Ubuntu 23.04+: sudo apt install libfuse2), D-Bus, and gnome-keyring or kwallet. Steps: 1) Place the .AppImage file in an 'Applications' folder. 2) Right-click the file and select 'Permissions'. 3) Check 'Allow executing file as a program'. Note: Officially supported on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS+ with GNOME or KDE. Lite Sync and right-click context menu not available on Linux. For Ubuntu startup, add to 'Startup Application Preferences'. For GNOME icon, install AppIndicator extension.
key_points: Lite Sync not available on Linux
actual_response:
To install kDrive on Linux, follow these steps:

### Prerequisites
- Ensure you are using **Ubuntu 22.04 LTS** or later with **GNOME** or **KDE** desktop environments.
- Download the kDrive AppImage file for Linux.
- Install the required dependencies:
  - **Fuse2**: Required to run AppImage. Install it using:
    ```bash
    sudo apt install libfuse2
    ```
  - **D-Bus**
  - **Gnome-keyring** or **kwallet** (usually pre-installed except on some lightweight distributions).

### Installation Steps
1. Place the downloaded AppImage file in a folder, for example, "Applications".
2. Right-click on the file and select **Permissions**.
3. Check the box **"Allow executing file as a program"**.

### Additional Operations
- **Ubuntu**: To run kDrive at startup, add the file to "Startup Application Preferences".
- **Gnome**: If the icon is missing, install [AppIndicator](https://extensions.gnome.org/extension/615/appindicator-support/).

For more details, refer to the official guide: [Install kDrive on Linux](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/617/install-kdrive-on-linux).

question: How can I share a file from kDrive?
ground_truth: To share a file/folder in kDrive: 1) Access kDrive web app at ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive. 2) Right-click on the file/folder. 3) Click 'Share...' at the top of the menu. Options: a) Activate a public share link (with options for modification, expiration date, password, download authorization). b) Or enter a kDrive user, contact email, or work team. For each person, define rights: 'viewing', 'modification', or 'management'. Recipients without Infomaniak account can create one free. Warning: deactivating/reactivating public link changes the URL.
key_points: recipients can create free Infomaniak account
actual_response:
To share a file from kDrive, follow these steps:

1. Access the kDrive web app by clicking [here](https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive).
2. Right-click on the file or folder you want to share.
3. Click on **Share** at the top of the dropdown menu.

From there, you have two options:

### Option 1: Public Share Link
- Activate the **public share link**.
- Customize the sharing options:

question: What is a Drop Box in kDrive and how do I create one?
ground_truth: A Drop Box in kDrive lets you invite contacts to deposit files/folders directly into your kDrive. To create: 1) Access kDrive at ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive. 2) Navigate to the folder that will host the data (personal or shared). 3) Click the blue 'New' button. 4) Click 'Drop Box'. 5) Enter a name. 6) Choose access settings. 7) Click 'Create'. 8) Share the link with contacts. Advanced options: email notification on deposit, password protection, expiration date, storage limit. To disable: go to Shares > Drop boxes, right-click and select 'Disable' (converts to regular folder).
key_points: can set password, expiration, storage limit
actual_response:
A **Drop Box** in kDrive is a feature that allows you to create a dedicated folder where external contacts can upload files or folders directly into your kDrive. This is useful for collecting content from others without giving them full access to your kDrive.

### How to Create a Drop Box in kDrive:

1. **Access kDrive**:
   - Go to the [kDrive Web app](https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive).

2. **Navigate to the Desired Folder**:
   - Choose the folder where you want the Drop Box to be created (either in your personal folder or a shared folder).

3. **Create the Drop Box**:
   - Click the **New** button.
   - Select **Drop Box** from the menu.
   - Enter a **name** for the Drop Box.
   - Confirm the location path.
   - Choose whether to restrict access to your user only or allow others in shared folders to view the content.
   - Click **Create**.

4. **Share the Drop Box**:
   - Share the link to the Drop Box or send it via email.
   - You can customize advanced options such as email notifications, password protection, expiration date, and storage limits.

5. **Customize Appearance (Optional)**:
   - You can customize the appearance of the Drop Box by adding a background image or changing the text color to match your organization's branding.

For more details, refer to the [official guide on managing kDrive Drop Boxes](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2386/manage-kdrive-drop-boxes).

question: How do I resolve sync conflicts in kDrive?
ground_truth: Sync conflicts occur when: a file is modified locally AND on kDrive Web simultaneously, or during conflicting create/move operations. Resolution: kDrive Web version is kept, local version is saved as '[filename]_conflict'. Options: 1) Keep both (only original syncs). 2) Delete _conflict if it's older. 3) Delete original and rename _conflict to sync it. 4) Manually merge then delete _conflict. To view conflicts: click kDrive icon > info button > view events. From version 3.6.11, locally modified files are moved to 'kDrive Rescue Folder' instead of deleted. Avoid conflicts by not working on the same file with multiple people.
key_points: conflicts when same file modified locally and online
can keep both, delete, or merge
actual_response:
To resolve sync conflicts in kDrive, follow these steps:

### Displaying Conflicts
1. Left-click on the kDrive desktop app icon in your computer's notification area.
2. Click on the information button at the top.
3. Click on the listed event to view its details.
4. Conflicts and errors are displayed in two distinct tabs, allowing you to identify unsynchronized data.

### Resolving Conflicts
1. Choose how to resolve the conflict:
   - Send the local version to the server (synchronize).
   - Move the local version to the computer's recycle bin.

### Manual Resolution
If conflicts are not resolved automatically:
1. Open both files.
2. Compare the differences.
3. Retrieve the information from the conflict file (marked with an exclamation mark) into the base file.
4. Delete the conflict file that is not synchronized.

### Best Practices to Avoid Conflicts
- Avoid working on the same file with multiple people simultaneously (unless using online tools like Word, Excel, or PowerPoint).
- Synchronize offline modifications before making changes online.
- Avoid creating folders with the same name as folders you do not synchronize on a device.

For more details, refer to the [official guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2403/resolve-a-kdrive-synchronization-conflict).

question: How do I manage user rights in kDrive?
ground_truth: kDrive has 2 permission levels: 1) Administrator - same rights as owner (sharing, statistics, restore/delete folders, import data, access all files). 2) User - access folders at root, create/share content, but cannot manage product, view statistics, or create root folders. To modify: 1) Go to ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive. 2) Click action menu next to the kDrive. 3) Click 'Manage users'. 4) Select user and choose access level. Note: Don't confuse Manager rights (product management) with kDrive rights (data access). A user can have restricted Manager rights but be Administrator in kDrive.
key_points: don't confuse Manager rights with kDrive rights
actual_response:
To manage user rights in kDrive, follow these steps:

1. **Access kDrive**:
   - Go to the [Infomaniak kDrive Web app](https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/kdrive).
   - Select the relevant kDrive from the dropdown menu in the left sidebar.

2. **Manage User Rights**:
   - Click on the **action menu ⋮** next to the relevant item.
   - Select **Manage users**.
   - Choose the desired access level for the user:
     - **Administrator**: Grants full rights, including sharing, statistics, and managing folders.
     - **User**: Allows access to shared folders and personal directories but restricts administrative tasks.

3. **Modify Permissions**:
   - If you cannot modify a user's rights, adjust their role at the **Organization level**:
     - Reduce their role from **Administrator** to **User** if necessary.

4. **Advanced Actions**:
   - Use the **action menu ⋮** for additional options like blocking access or removing a user from kDrive.

5. **Understand Permission Levels**:
   - **View**: Allows viewing, downloading, and commenting.
   - **Modify**: Includes editing, adding, and deleting files.
   - **Manage**: Grants full control, including sharing and managing user rights (only for common folders).

For more details, refer to the [official guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2365/manage-a-kdrive-users-rights).

question: How can I access kDrive files locally without downloading them?
ground_truth: To access kDrive files locally: 1) Install the kDrive desktop app. 2) Click on the kDrive icon in notification area (top right macOS, bottom right Windows, double-click on Linux). 3) Click action menu at top right. 4) Choose 'Open kDrive Web' to access server files. 5) Or click the item above to open the local folder. Files can be physically present or virtually present (if Lite Sync is enabled). Lite Sync allows files to appear locally without taking up disk space - they download on demand when opened.
key_points: Open kDrive Web for server files
actual_response:
You can access your kDrive files locally without downloading them by using the **Lite Sync** feature in the kDrive desktop app. This feature allows you to view and manage files directly from your computer without taking up storage space, as the files remain stored in the cloud and are only downloaded when needed.

### Steps to Enable Lite Sync:
1. Install the [kDrive desktop app](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2374) on your device.
2. Open the kDrive app and click on the app icon in the notification area of your computer.
3. Click on the action menu **⋮** at the top right.
4. Enable the **Lite Sync** option to access files virtually without downloading them.

### Notes:
- Files will appear in a "dehydrated" state locally and will require a brief loading time when accessed.
- You can still view, edit, and synchronize files without using significant hard drive space.

For more details, refer to the guides for [Windows](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2562) or [macOS](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2608).

Source: [Access kDrive files locally and online](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2456)

question: How do I sync kDrive with my Synology NAS?
ground_truth: To sync kDrive with Synology NAS via WebDAV: Prerequisites: Synology NAS accessible from Internet, know your kDrive ID. Steps: 1) Log in to Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM). 2) Install Cloud Sync from Package Center if needed. 3) Open Cloud Sync. 4) Click + to add a Cloud. 5) Choose WebDAV. 6) Enter: Server address: https://[kDriveID].connect.kdrive.infomaniak.com, Username: Infomaniak email, Password: create an application password. 7) Select local folder, destination, and sync type: Bidirectional (changes in both directions), Download remote only (backup kDrive to NAS), or Download local only (backup NAS to kDrive).
key_points: Bidirectional, Download remote, or Download local sync
actual_response:
To sync kDrive with your Synology NAS, follow these steps:

1. **Prerequisites:**
   - Ensure your Synology NAS is accessible from the Internet.
   - Know your kDrive identifier (kDrive ID). You can find it [here](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2409).

2. **Steps to Sync:**
   - Log in to the Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM).
   - If necessary, download and install the **Cloud Sync** app from the **Package Center**.
   - Open **Cloud Sync**.
   - Click on the **+** at the bottom left to add a Cloud.
   - Choose **WebDAV** from the list of available Clouds.
   - Enter the following account parameters:
     - **Server address:** `https://IDkDrive.connect.kdrive.infomaniak.com` (replace `IDkDrive` with your kDrive ID)
     - **Username:** Your email address to log in to the Infomaniak account
     - **Password:** Create an application password for this specific use
   - Select the local folder, destination, and desired synchronization type:
     - **Bidirectional:** Changes made will be reflected in both directions.
     - **Download only remote changes:** Ideal for saving a kDrive to your NAS.
     - **Download only local changes:** Ideal for saving data from your NAS to a kDrive.

For more details, refer to the [official guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2404/sync-synology-with-kdrive).

question: How do I create a channel in kChat?
ground_truth: To create a channel in kChat: 1) Click the button in the left sidebar of kChat web app (ksuite.infomaniak.com/kchat). 2) Click 'Create a new channel'. 3) Set: A) Name (modifiable later), B) URL (lowercase, numbers, dots, dashes, underscores), C) Private or Public status, D) Description. Every Organization has a default 'General' channel for all users. Public channels are visible to all; Private channels require invitation. To convert public to private: click channel > chevron > Convert (permanent). To leave: chevron > Leave. To archive: chevron > Archive. Can also add to favorites, mute, or organize by categories.
actual_response:
To create a channel in kChat, follow these steps:

1. Open the **kChat** web app: [ksuite.infomaniak.com/kchat](https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/kchat).
2. Click on the button located in the left sidebar.
3. Select **Create a new channel**.
4. Configure the channel by setting:

question: What slash commands are available in kChat?
ground_truth: To use slash commands in kChat: 1) Click in the composition field. 2) Type / followed by the command. 3) Send. Typing just / shows available commands in a modal (like going offline). You can create custom slash commands: 1) Open kChat web or desktop app. 2) Click 'New' icon next to organization name. 3) Click 'Integrations'. 4) Click 'Slash command'. 5) Add a command with name, trigger, content type, and action. Custom commands can call external APIs or run scripts. Note: External users cannot see the Integrations menu.
actual_response:
Here are the available slash commands in kChat:

- **Execute a slash command**:
  - Click in the composition field within a channel.
  - Enter a `/` (slash or forward slash) followed by the command.
  - Confirm to send the command.
  - Typing only `/` will display a modal with available commands, such as going offline.

- **Create a custom slash command**:
  - Access the Web kChat app or the desktop kChat app.
  - Click on the **New** icon next to your kChat organization name.
  - Click on **Integrations**.
  - Click on **Slash command**.
  - Click the blue button to **Add a command**.
  - Configure the slash command (name, trigger, expected content type, action to execute, etc.).
  - Save the command and test it to ensure it works as expected.

For more details, refer to the [kChat slash commands documentation](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2134/using-kchat-slash-commands).

question: How can I connect external applications to kChat?
ground_truth: To connect external apps to kChat using webhooks: 1) Open kChat web or desktop app. 2) Click 'New' icon next to organization name. 3) Click 'Integrations'. 4) Access webhook categories. For incoming webhooks (receive messages from external apps): 1) Click 'Incoming Webhooks'. 2) Add name and description. 3) Select destination channel. 4) Save to get URL. 5) External app sends POST request with JSON: {"text": "message"}. For outgoing webhooks: kChat sends info when events occur. Parameters include channel override, username, icon_url. Response includes message details. Add ?slack_return_format=true for Slack-style response.
key_points: Incoming webhooks receive from external apps
Outgoing webhooks send to external apps
POST request with JSON text field
actual_response:
To connect external applications to kChat, you can use webhooks. Here’s how you can do it:

### Steps to Connect External Applications to kChat:

1. **Access the kChat Webhooks Interface**:
   - Open the **kChat** web app or desktop app.
   - Click on the **New** icon next to your kChat organization's name.
   - Select **Integrations**.
   - Choose the category **Incoming Webhooks**.

2. **Create an Incoming Webhook**:
   - Click on the blue button **Add incoming webhooks**.
   - Add a name and description for the webhook.
   - Select the channel that will receive the messages.
   - Save to generate the webhook URL (keep this URL private).

3. **Configure the External Application**:
   - Use the generated webhook URL in the external application to send data to kChat.
   - Adjust the request format according to the provided URL. For example:
     ```json
     {
         "text": "Hello, text1\nText2."
     }
     ```
   - Optionally, you can use `curl` to test the webhook:
     ```bash
     curl -i -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"text": "Hello, text1\nText2."}' https://your-server-kchat.xyz/hooks/xxx-key-generated-xxx
     ```

4. **Additional Parameters**:
   - You can customize the message with additional parameters like `channel`, `username`, and `icon_url`. For example:
     ```json
     {
         "channel": "kchatemp",
         "username": "test-automation",
         "icon_url": "https://domain.xyz/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/icon.png",
         "text": "#### Results of tests for July 27, 2023\n@channel please check the failed tests."
     }
     ```

### Notes:
- If you want the response format to match Slack, add `?slack_return_format=true` to the webhook URL.
- The BOT indication will appear next to the username on kChat for security reasons.

For more details, refer to the [official documentation](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2001/connect-external-applications-to-kchat).

question: How do I translate a message in kChat?
ground_truth: To translate a message in kChat: 1) Access kChat via ksuite.infomaniak.com/kchat, or the mobile app (iOS/Android), or desktop app (macOS/Windows/Linux). 2) View the message to translate. 3) Click the action menu (three dots) at the top right of the message. 4) Click 'Translate'. 5) The translated message appears below your conversation and is only visible to you. The translation is automatic into your own language.
key_points: click action menu (three dots) on message
actual_response:
To translate a message in kChat, follow these steps:

1. Open the **kChat** web app, mobile app, or desktop app.
2. View the message you want to translate.
3. Click on the action menu (**•••**) located at the top right of the message.
4. Select **Translate**.
5. The translated message will appear below the conversation and will only be visible to you.

Source: [Translate the content of a message on the kChat Infomaniak app](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/1467/translate-the-content-of-a-message-on-the-kchat-infomaniak-app)

question: How can I invite external users to kChat?
ground_truth: To invite external users to kChat: Prerequisites: Be Organization administrator with full kChat rights. Steps: 1) Access kChat at ksuite.infomaniak.com/kchat or desktop app. 2) Click 'Invite members' button. 3) Click link to invite new user. 4) Enter email address(es). 5) Specify channel(s) they'll access. 6) Click send invitation. Invited users receive email with link to the channel. They must create Infomaniak account if needed. External users are not counted as regular users. Guests CAN: pin messages, use slash commands, add favorites, mute, update profile. Guests CANNOT: discover public channels, join open teams, create DMs with non-channel members, invite people.
key_points: external users not counted as users
actual_response:
To invite external users to kChat, follow these steps:

1. **Access kChat**:
   - Open the [kChat Web app](https://ksuite.infomaniak.com/kchat) or the kChat desktop app.

2. **Invite Members**:
   - Click the **Invite members** button.

3. **Invite a New User**:
   - Click the link to invite a new user.

4. **Specify Details**:
   - Enter the email address(es) of the person(s) you want to invite.
   - Specify the channel(s) to which these users will have access.

5. **Send the Invitation**:
   - Click the blue button to send the invitation.

6. **Registration**:
   - The invited person will receive an email with a link to the kChat interface and the shared channel.
   - If the user does not have an Infomaniak account, they will need to register.

7. **Access kChat**:
   - Once registered, the user can access kChat and the specified channel.

For more details, refer to the [official guide](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2846/invite-an-external-user-to-use-kchat).

question: What is Euria and how do I use it in kChat?
ground_truth: Euria is the AI assistant available in kSuite/kChat. It can perform calculations, translations, provide information, and answer questions. To use: 1) In kChat left sidebar, use channel search (bots appear as channels) or click + next to Direct Messages. 2) Search for 'bot' or the bot name. 3) Add the bot with [bot] tag. 4) Create a private discussion with the bot (not a group conversation). 5) Write to it like chatting with a person. New users automatically receive a welcome message from Euria. For AI summaries of discussions, refer to the separate summary feature guide.
key_points: Euria is AI assistant in kSuite
search for bot in channel search
actual_response:
### What is Euria?
Euria is an artificial intelligence integrated into Infomaniak's kSuite, designed to assist with tasks such as calculations, translations, providing information, and answering questions. It is particularly useful as a conversational agent in kChat and for summarizing discussions.

### How to Use Euria in kChat:
1. **Add Euria to Your Contacts**:
   - Euria is already available as a bot in your kChat contacts.
   - If you don’t see it, click on the channel search or the **+** icon next to **Direct Messages** to find it.
   - Start a private conversation with Euria by selecting it from your contacts.

2. **Interact with Euria**:
   - Simply type your questions or requests in the chat, and Euria will respond accordingly.

3. **Summarize Discussions**:
   - Hover over a message in kChat and click the Euria actions icon.
   - Select **Summarize the discussion thread** to get an AI-generated summary.

For more details, refer to the official guides:
- [Use Euria on kChat (conversational agent)](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2840/use-euria-on-kchat-conversational-agent)
- [Use Euria on kChat (summarize a discussion)](https://www.infomaniak.com/en/support/faq/2480/use-euria-on-kchat-summarize-a-discussion)
